tables.title: Metrological Comparison in Common Units
tables.intro: Each row compares the same quantity in the same units. Δ is evaluation minus reference; Δ/u expresses the difference in units of the stated uncertainty. Exact SI references have zero uncertainty, so that quotient is not defined.
tables.note: The reciprocal 1/α is compared directly with the same CODATA quantity. Against 2018, the relative difference is 7.78924 × 10⁻³⁵; the experimental uncertainty of 1/α is 2.1 × 10⁻⁸. The tabulated decimal α = 0.0072973525693(11) is rounded: its absolute difference is 1.61990 × 10⁻¹⁴ and is not a separate measurement. The electron uses uE = 1 MeV. Sources: I, VI, and NIST/CODATA 2018 and 2022.

tables.note: ℏgeom expresses the common scale; ℏret is the returned action used in Gret. The exact reduced reference is hSI/(2π). Rounding hgeom to nine significant figures gives 6.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴; the relative difference before rounding is −3.46643 × 10⁻¹⁰. The gravitational evaluation uses Lα = (5759/23040)α¹⁶ × 1 m, ℏret = ηret × 10⁻³⁴ J s, and c = 299792458 m/s. Length and G agree with the references within their uncertainties: u(lP) = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴⁰ m and u(G) = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵ m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻². CODATA derives its Planck length from G, so those references are related. Sources: II, the joint length–gravitation development, integral corpus equation (36.14), NIST/CODATA 2022, and BIPM.

tables.title: Boltzmann · Spectral Construction and Thermal Reading
tables.intro: The coefficient is obtained as a relative intensity of the marked spectral reference. The thermal reading combines information per reference and conditioned energy; their derivative fixes temperature in the transported bases.
tables.note: The comparison uses uE = 1 J and uΘ = 1 K; both columns therefore express energy per unit temperature. The numerical coefficient b* comes from the spectral realization described above. Ranks 1, 380, and 649, degrees 23 + 3n, and the rank-one reference specify the realization. Within it, additivity and conditioning determine the transducer and the free-energy minimum. The number exactly matches the SI numeral of Boltzmann’s constant; the physical identification retains these operations and the energy and temperature bases. Source: II, marked thermal composition and reading instrument; the SI reference is used after evaluation.

tables.title: CKM Mixing and the Barbero–Immirzi Coefficient
tables.intro: The five calculated CKM coordinates lie within the PDG 2025 reference intervals. Sines, CP phase, and Jarlskog invariant are compared in the same parametrization. Barbero–Immirzi is shown with the theoretical Ghosh–Mitra reference. Δ denotes evaluation minus reference.
tables.note: Sources: article II and the PDG 2025 CKM review, equations (12.27)–(12.28). Δ/u uses the published uncertainty on the side selected by the sign of Δ. The sines are matrix parameters; matrix elements also contain cosine factors. For γ, the relative difference from Ghosh–Mitra is −2.15953 × 10⁻⁴; this reference follows from its state-counting equation.

tables.title: CKM Angles Expressed in Degrees
tables.intro: To make the angular comparison explicit, the same coordinates as in the preceding table are expressed in degrees. The θ references are obtained by applying arcsin to the PDG 2025 sines; the CP phase is converted from radians. These are not additional measurements.
tables.note: The figures are rounded only for presentation. Angular uncertainties are obtained by transforming the endpoints of the published intervals; degrees are not identified with sines. Source: PDG 2025, CKM review, equations (12.27)–(12.28).

tables.title: Electroweak Angular Reading and the On-Shell Reference
tables.intro: W and Z share the counter-angle and differ by one angle unit. Their angular ratio retains exp(−x), while the complete signatures also contain Δ₄, s₁₂₀, and ζ₂₇₀. Subtracting (94, −1, 0, −2, 4) and (95, −1, −11, 0, −4) preserves these terms and changes the ratio. Electroweak mixing is distinct from CKM mixing.
tables.note: The second row uses the complete-signature masses in the final table: mW = 80378.964909704547… and mZ = 91187.533444313408… MeV/c². On-shell defines sW² = 1 − MW²/MZ² for physical masses in that convention; the PDG fit includes radiative effects. The differences are 16.1209 and −4.52478 reference uncertainties. They are numerical distances; the physical comparison retains the signature realization and pole or resonance convention. The angular determinant does not replace the complete mass ratio. Sources: VI, the narrative W/Z section, and PDG 2025 §§10.2 and 10.4.5.

tables.title: Electromagnetic Constants in SI Units
tables.intro: The HMT evaluation and the references are expressed in the same units. Both CODATA editions are retained to show the agreement with 2018 and the change in the 2022 adjustment. Δ means evaluation minus reference.
tables.note: The documented realization uses α_HMT and the exact defining values of the SI: h_SI = 6.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e_SI = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and c_SI = 299792458 m/s. Here e_SI is the elementary charge. CODATA enters subsequently, as a reference; the three electromagnetic comparisons depend on the same evaluation of α. Equality of c expresses the adopted SI convention, not an independent prediction. The normalized coefficients of the constitutive derivation are not compared directly with dimensional quantities. Sources: integral corpus, p. 119, and NIST/CODATA 2018–2022. Parentheses indicate standard uncertainty.

comparison_conventions.normalized_residual: (x_HMT - x_ref) / u_ref; for asymmetric uncertainty, use u_plus for a positive difference and u_minus for a negative difference.
comparison_conventions.exact_references: For exact SI references, normalized_residual is null: division by zero uncertainty is not defined.
comparison_conventions.numerical_method: The inherited rows retain their documented precision. New length, returned-action, and G differences are checked with 90-digit decimal arithmetic on the previously reproduced coordinates; stored residuals are rounded. No additional experimental precision is attributed to these evaluations.
comparison_conventions.interpretation: A marginal normalized residual is neither a probability nor a global goodness-of-fit test. Squares are not summed without covariances. Additional evaluation digits do not reduce experimental uncertainty.
comparison_conventions.cross_editions: CODATA 2018 and 2022 adjustments are retained for alpha, the electron, and electromagnetic constants; they are not independent determinations.
comparison_conventions.Planck_length_reference: The tabulated Planck length is derived from the reference G with exact SI hbar and c; the length and G residuals are not independent experimental tests.

editorial_instructions: Preserve the formula and value of h as well as ℏ. Do not replace the formula by h = 2πℏ alone.
Show α–CODATA 2018 and electron–CODATA 2022 together, retaining in notes or secondary columns the cross-edition comparisons already present in article I.
For CKM, compare sin θij, δ in radians, and J; do not confuse sin θ12 with |Vus| or sin θ23 with |Vcb|.
For G, distinguish the marked-length evaluation with returned action, the historical chart numeral, and the subsequent CODATA reference; never fill the output column with the reference.
Present internal coefficients and SI references in separate tables. Do not subtract quantities of different dimensions or use the target to select a scale and manufacture a comparison.
Retain the on-shell row despite the discrepancy; identify the observable and comparator edition.
Do not turn a calculated decimal, an exact SI reference, or a small marginal residual into a global experimental certificate.
Present action, reduced action, marked length, and Planck scales before the electromagnetic block. Keep quantum mixing before electromagnetism and the thermal section with length and scales.
